definitions.TV: one half the l1 probability difference

method: Exact fixed-t bivariate cumulant recurrence, odd/even exponential Taylor bounds, rational square-root enclosures, factorial-moment tail bound, and product-affinity inequalities.

parameters.interpretation: An exact mathematical operating point, not a physical detector calibration or recommended experiment.

full_count_samples_95.scope: Known competing models; independent count snapshots. Necessary and sufficient bounds enclose, but do not determine, the exact optimal sample count.

four_count_samples_95.scope: Known competing models; independent count snapshots. Necessary and sufficient bounds enclose, but do not determine, the exact optimal sample count.

explicit_four_count_threshold_rule.rule: For m independent snapshots, choose B if the fraction with N=4 exceeds the threshold; choose A otherwise.

four_count_blind_gain.function: F(eta)=E_A[I^4 exp(-eta I)]-E_B[I^4 exp(-eta I)]; count-four gap=eta^4 F(eta)/24
four_count_blind_gain.conclusion: Exactly one simple four-count blind gain in this interval. At this gain the Bernoulli four-count indicator has identical laws for A and B. Full photon-count laws remain different by their fourth factorial moments.
four_count_blind_gain.scope: Local uniqueness only; no global count of blind gains or full-detector optimum is claimed.

finite_small_noise_bound_example.scope: A nonasymptotic demonstration of the six-moment bound, not a practical sample-size recommendation.

limitations: No external peer review or experimental calibration.
Sample bounds do not give exact optimal sample counts or acquisition times.
Four-count blind gain is locally unique; global uniqueness is not established.
The numeric operating points are mathematical examples, not proposed laboratory settings.
Every snapshot must be independent conditional on the unknown structure, with the stated common parameters.
